enhanced.fullText:
The Consumer Credit Protection Act, Title III (CCPA), codified at 15 U.S.C. §§ 1671-1677, establishes federal limitations on wage garnishment and prohibits discriminatory employment practices related to garnishment orders. This federal law applies to all employers, including higher education institutions, that pay wages subject to garnishment orders issued by state or federal courts.

Under 15 U.S.C. § 1673, the maximum amount of an employee's disposable earnings subject to garnishment in any workweek cannot exceed the lesser of: (1) 25% of the employee's disposable earnings for that week, or (2) the amount by which disposable earnings exceed 30 times the federal minimum wage ($7.25 as of 2023, making the threshold $217.50 per week). Disposable earnings are defined as compensation paid or payable after deduction of amounts required by law, including federal and state taxes, Social Security, and unemployment insurance.

Critical anti-retaliation provisions under 15 U.S.C. § 1674 strictly prohibit higher education institutions from discharging, disciplining, or discriminating against any employee because their earnings have been subjected to garnishment for any one indebtedness. Violations result in a fine up to $1,000 per violation and potential reinstatement obligations. The Department of Labor's Wage and Hour Division enforces these provisions under 29 CFR Part 870.

Higher education institutions must implement compliant payroll procedures to calculate garnishment amounts correctly, considering multiple garnishment orders and priority requirements. Student loan garnishments under the Higher Education Act may be subject to additional federal requirements under 34 CFR Part 682. Institutions processing federal payroll must ensure compliance with both Title III limitations and specific federal employee garnishment procedures under 5 CFR Part 581.

The CCPA preempts state garnishment laws only when state provisions allow greater garnishment amounts than federal limits. When state laws provide greater employee protection, state law applies. Universities operating in multiple states must maintain compliance systems accommodating varying state requirements while adhering to federal minimum protections.

Recent regulatory updates include clarification of disposable income calculations and electronic garnishment processing requirements. The Department of Labor continues to issue guidance on implementation, particularly regarding administrative wage garnishments and federal benefit payments.
enhanced.summary: CCPA Title III limits employee wage garnishments to 25% of disposable earnings or amounts exceeding 30x federal minimum wage weekly, whichever is less, and prohibits employment discrimination based on garnishment status with $1,000 penalties.
enhanced.requirements:
## Garnishment Calculation Compliance
- Calculate maximum garnishment as lesser of 25% disposable earnings or amount exceeding $217.50 weekly
- Implement payroll systems ensuring accurate disposable earnings calculations after required legal deductions
- Establish procedures for handling multiple garnishment orders with proper priority sequencing

## Anti-Retaliation Protections
- Prohibit discharge, discipline, or discrimination against employees subject to garnishment for single indebtedness
- Train HR personnel on 15 U.S.C. § 1674 compliance requirements and $1,000 penalty provisions
- Document garnishment-related employment decisions to demonstrate compliance

## Multi-State Operations
- Review state garnishment laws in all operating jurisdictions for employee-favorable provisions
- Implement systems applying most protective garnishment limitations between federal and state law
- Maintain current knowledge of state law changes affecting garnishment calculations
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No routine federal reporting required under CCPA Title III. Institutions must respond to Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division investigations within specified timeframes and maintain payroll records demonstrating garnishment calculation compliance for DOL review upon request.
